newsitem.title: USA: Insurers blast California's stance on quake claims.
newsitem.headline: Insurers blast California's stance on quake claims.

text.p: Insurance companies accused California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush of ignoring state law on Monday after he called on the companies to pay the late claims of homeowners hit by the 1994 Northridge earthquake.

"Apparently the commissioner either doesn't know the law or is choosing to ignore it," said Dan Dunmoyer, president of the Personal Insurance Federation of California, which represents major insurance companies in the state.

Earlier on Monday, Quackenbush issued a legal opinion calling on insurance companies to pay the late claims of hundreds of homeowners even though the damages were discovered long after the January 1994 earthquake.
Quackenbush said the opinion would help bring to a close at least 450 late insurance claim cases stemming from the Northridge earthquake.
The Northridge earthquake, which had a 6.8-magnitude, killed more than 50 people and caused billions of dollars in damage throughout the Los Angeles area.
State law prohibits insurance claims from being filed more than a year after damage has occurred, the Personal Insurance Federation of California said in a statement.
"That's the law and we wonder why the commissioner has come forward three years and four months after Northridge to make these charges," Dunmoyer said.
